biodiversity_overview.text: 6,177 GBIF occurrence records for 43 tracked species are attributed to Punjab, spanning 1926-2026.
6,129 of these records (99.2%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 22, Magnoliopsida 7, Mammalia 6, Squamata 3, Testudines 3, Amphibia 2.

threatened_species.text: 5 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Pied Starling (1,039), Indian Grey-Hornbill (988), Indian Spot-billed Duck (856), White-throated Munia (594), Common Peafowl (501).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 82 in 2016 to 25 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 0.55% of Punjab's area (14 areas intersect the state).
4.6% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (280 of 6,129); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Spotted Creeper (0.49), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47), Green Turtle (0.40), Indian Roofed Turtle (0.36), Indian Gooseberry (0.35).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Punjab (equal-weight reference): cell near 30.375N 76.875E (overall rank 36, median rank across weightings 55); cell near 31.125N 76.125E (overall rank 68, median rank across weightings 86); cell near 30.375N 76.125E (overall rank 144, median rank across weightings 158).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 816 km2 (1.58% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

14.7 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (1.8% of the 2000 extent; 0.27% in 2015-2024, rank 23 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2005 (1.44 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 2.99% of land and population density is 618.4 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
42% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
